title: Arakhin 32
description: Chapter 9, HaMokher Sadehu, continues: whether payment against the recipient’s will counts as giving, what inside a city wall counts as a house, a house built into the wall, which cities count as walled from the days of Joshua, and whether Joshua’s consecration of the land lasted forever or only for its time.
topics: 💰 Hillel’s ordinance: is giving against the recipient’s will a valid act of giving?
🏘️ Olive presses, bathhouses and dovecotes, a quarry and a sand bed: like houses or like fields?
🧱 A house built into the wall: Rahab’s house and “she dwelt upon the wall”
🏰 A walled city: three courtyards of two houses, a real wall and not roofs, and not Tiberias, whose wall is the sea
🗺️ Gamla in the Galilee, Gedod in Transjordan, and two Jerusalems
✡️ Did the first consecration of the land last forever, or only for its time?
⛺ “Since the days of Joshua”: sukkot in Ezra’s day, and Yeshua instead of Yehoshua
📅 Counting Jubilees after the tribes were exiled, to keep the Sabbatical Years in their place

a1.he: מִדְּאִיצְטְרִיךְ לֵיהּ לְהִלֵּל לְתַקּוֹנֵי נְתִינָה בְּעַל כׇּרְחוֹ הָוְיָא נְתִינָה, הָא בְּעָלְמָא נְתִינָה בְּעַל כׇּרְחוֹ לָא הָוְיָא נְתִינָה.

a2.he: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב פָּפָּא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב אָשֵׁי: וְדִילְמָא כִּי אִיצְטְרִיכָא לֵיהּ לְהִלֵּל לְתַקּוֹנֵי שֶׁלֹּא בְּפָנָיו, אֲבָל בְּפָנָיו — בֵּין מִדַּעְתּוֹ בֵּין בְּעַל כׇּרְחוֹ הָוְיָא מַתָּנָה!

a3.he: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי, אָמַר רָבָא: מִתַּקָּנָתוֹ שֶׁל הִלֵּל — ״הֲרֵי זֶה גִּיטִּיךְ עַל מְנָת שֶׁתִּתְּנִי לִי מָאתַיִם זוּז״, וּנְתָנָהּ לוֹ, בֵּין מִדַּעְתּוֹ בֵּין בְּעַל כׇּרְחוֹ — הָוְיָא נְתִינָה. וְכִי אִיצְטְרִיךְ לֵיהּ לְהִלֵּל לְתַקּוֹנֵי — שֶׁלֹּא בְּפָנָיו, אֲבָל בְּפָנָיו — בֵּין מִדַּעְתּוֹ בֵּין בְּעַל כׇּרְחוֹ הָוְיָא נְתִינָה.

a4.he: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב פָּפָּא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב שִׁימִי בַּר אָשֵׁי: וְדִילְמָא בֵּין בְּפָנָיו בֵּין שֶׁלֹּא בְּפָנָיו, מִדַּעְתּוֹ — אִין, בְּעַל כׇּרְחוֹ — לָא, וְהִלֵּל מַאי דְּאִיצְטְרִיךְ לֵיהּ תַּקֵּין!

a5.he: מַתְנִי׳ כׇּל שֶׁהוּא לִפְנִים מִן הַחוֹמָה — הֲרֵי הוּא כְּבָתֵּי עָרֵי חוֹמָה, חוּץ מִן הַשָּׂדוֹת. רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: אַף הַשָּׂדוֹת. בַּיִת הַבָּנוּי בַּחוֹמָה — רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אֵינוֹ כְּבָתֵּי עָרֵי חוֹמָה. רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: כּוֹתֶל הַחִיצוֹן הִיא חוֹמָתוֹ.

a6.he: גְּמָ׳ תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: בַּיִת — אֵין לִי אֶלָּא בַּיִת, מִנַּיִן לְרַבּוֹת בָּתֵּי בַדִּים וּבָתֵּי מֶרְחֲצָאוֹת וּמִגְדָּלוֹת וְשׁוֹבָכִין וּבוֹרוֹת וְשִׁיחִין וּמְעָרוֹת? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״אֲשֶׁר בָּעִיר״. יָכוֹל שֶׁאֲנִי מְרַבֶּה אַף הַשָּׂדוֹת? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״בַּיִת״, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה.

a7.he: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: נֶאֱמַר ״בַּיִת״ — אֵין לִי אֶלָּא בַּיִת, מִנַּיִן לְרַבּוֹת בָּתֵּי בַדִּים וּבָתֵּי מֶרְחֲצָאוֹת, וּמִגְדָּלוֹת וְשׁוֹבָכִין, וּבוֹרוֹת שִׁיחִין וּמְעָרוֹת, וַאֲפִילּוּ שָׂדוֹת? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״אֲשֶׁר בָּעִיר״.

a8.he: וְאֶלָּא הָא כְּתִיב ״בַּיִת״! אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר רַב קַטִּינָא: חוֹלְסִית וּמְצוּלָה אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ, וְהָתַנְיָא: חוֹלְסִית וּמְצוּלָה, רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: כְּבָתִּים, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: כְּשָׂדוֹת.

a9.he: בַּיִת הַבָּנוּי בַּחוֹמָה, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אֵינוֹ כְּבָתֵּי עָרֵי חוֹמָה. אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: וּשְׁנֵיהֶם מִקְרָא אֶחָד דָּרְשׁוּ, ״וַתּוֹרִידֵם בַּחֶבֶל בְּעַד הַחַלּוֹן כִּי בֵיתָהּ בְּקִיר הַחוֹמָה וּבַחוֹמָה הִיא יוֹשָׁבֶת״. רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סָבַר כִּפְשָׁטֵיהּ דִּקְרָא, וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר: ״בַּחוֹמָה הִיא יוֹשָׁבֶת״ וְלֹא בְּעִיר חוֹמָה.

a10.he: מַתְנִי׳ עִיר שֶׁגַּגּוֹתֶיהָ חוֹמָתָהּ, וְשֶׁאֵינָהּ מוּקֶּפֶת חוֹמָה מִימוֹת יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בִּן נוּן, אֵינָהּ כְּבָתֵּי עָרֵי חוֹמָה. וְאֵלּוּ הֵן בָּתֵּי עָרֵי חוֹמָה: שָׁלֹשׁ חֲצֵרוֹת שֶׁל שְׁנֵי בָתִּים, מוּקֶּפֶת חוֹמָה מִימוֹת יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בִּן נוּן, כְּגוֹן קַצְרָה הַיְּשָׁנָה שֶׁל צִיפּוֹרִי, וְחַקְרָה שֶׁל גּוּשׁ חָלָב, וְיוֹדְפַת הַיְּשָׁנָה, וְגַמְלָא, וּגְדוֹד, וְחָדִיד, וְאוֹנוֹ, וִירוּשָׁלַיִם, וְכֵן כְּיוֹצֵא בָּהֶן.

a11.he: גְּמָ׳ תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״חוֹמָה״ — וְלֹא שׁוּר אִיגָּר, ״סָבִיב״ — פְּרָט לִטְבֶרְיָה שֶׁיַּמָּהּ חוֹמָתָהּ.

a12.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בַּר יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: ״אֲשֶׁר לוֹא חוֹמָה״ — אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ עַכְשָׁיו וְהָיָה לוֹ קוֹדֶם לָכֵן.

a13.he: וְאֵלּוּ הֵן בָּתֵּי עָרֵי חוֹמָה כּוּ׳. תָּנָא: גַּמְלָא בַּגָּלִיל, וּגְדוֹד בְּעֵבֶר הַיַּרְדֵּן, וְחָדִיד וְאוֹנוֹ וִירוּשָׁלַיִם בִּיהוּדָה. מַאי קָאָמַר?

b1.he: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הָכִי קָאָמַר — עַד גַּמְלָא בַּגָּלִיל, עַד גְּדוֹד בְּעֵבֶר הַיַּרְדֵּן, וְחָדִיד וְאוֹנוֹ וִירוּשָׁלַיִם בִּיהוּדָה.

b2.he: רָבָא אָמַר: גַּמְלָא בַּגָּלִיל, לְאַפּוֹקֵי גַּמְלָא דִּשְׁאָר אֲרָצוֹת; גְּדוֹד בְּעֵבֶר הַיַּרְדֵּן, לְאַפּוֹקֵי גְּדוֹד דִּשְׁאָר אֲרָצוֹת; אִינָךְ דְּלָא אִיכָּא דִּכְוָתַיְיהוּ — לָא אִיצְטְרִיךְ לֵיהּ.

b3.he: וִירוּשָׁלַיִם מִי מִיחֲלַט בַּהּ? וְהָתַנְיָא: עֲשָׂרָה דְּבָרִים נֶאֶמְרוּ בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם, אֵין הַבַּיִת חָלוּט בָּהּ!

b4.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: כִּירוּשָׁלַיִם דְּמוּקֶּפֶת חוֹמָה מִימוֹת יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בִּן נוּן, וְלֹא כִּירוּשָׁלַיִם, דְּאִילּוּ יְרוּשָׁלַיִם אֵין הַבַּיִת חָלוּט בָּהּ, וְאִילּוּ הָכָא הַבַּיִת חָלוּט (בהן) [בָּהּ]. רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: לָאו אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף תְּרֵי קָדֵשׁ הֲווֹ? הָכָא נָמֵי תְּרֵי יְרוּשָׁלַיִם הֲווֹ.

b5.he: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי: לָמָּה מָנוּ חֲכָמִים אֶת אֵלּוּ, שֶׁכְּשֶׁעָלוּ בְּנֵי הַגּוֹלָה מָצְאוּ אֵלּוּ וְקִידְּשׁוּם, אֲבָל רִאשׁוֹנוֹת בָּטְלוּ מִשֶּׁבָּטְלָה קְדוּשַּׁת הָאָרֶץ. קָסָבַר: קְדוּשָּׁה רִאשׁוֹנָה קִידְּשָׁה לִשְׁעָתָהּ, וְלֹא קִידְּשָׁה לֶעָתִיד לָבֹא.

b6.he: וּרְמִינְהִי: אָמַר רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי: וְכִי אֵלּוּ בִּלְבַד הָיוּ? וַהֲלֹא כְּבָר נֶאֱמַר: ״שִׁשִּׁים עִיר כׇּל חֶבֶל אַרְגּוֹב... כׇּל אֵלֶּה עָרִים בְּצוּרוֹת״! אֶלָּא לָמָּה מָנוּ חֲכָמִים אֶת אֵלּוּ? שֶׁכְּשֶׁעָלוּ בְּנֵי הַגּוֹלָה מָצְאוּ אֵלּוּ וְקִידְּשׁוּם. קִידְּשׁוּם? הָא אָמְרִינַן דְּלָא צְרִיךְ לְקַדּוֹשִׁינְהוּ! אֶלָּא מְנָאוּם.

b7.he: וְלֹא אֵלּוּ בִּלְבַד, אֶלָּא כֹּל שֶׁתַּעֲלֶה לְךָ מָסוֹרֶת בְּיָדְךָ מֵאֲבוֹתֶיךָ שֶׁמּוּקֶּפֶת חוֹמָה מִימוֹת יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בִּן נוּן — כׇּל מִצְוֹת הַלָּלוּ נוֹהֲגוֹת בָּהּ, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁקְּדוּשָּׁה רִאשׁוֹנָה קִידְּשָׁה לִשְׁעָתָהּ וְקִידְּשָׁה לֶעָתִיד לָבֹא!

b8.he: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: תְּרֵי תַּנָּאֵי וְאַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל, וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: חַד מִינַּיְיהוּ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר יוֹסֵי אַמְרַהּ, דְּתַנְיָא: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בַּר יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: ״אֲשֶׁר לוֹא חוֹמָה״ — אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ עַכְשָׁיו וְהָיָה לוֹ קוֹדֶם לָכֵן.

b9.he: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּמַאן דְּאָמַר: קְדוּשָּׁה רִאשׁוֹנָה קִידְּשָׁה לִשְׁעָתָהּ וְלֹא קִידְּשָׁה לֶעָתִיד לָבֹא? דִּכְתִיב: ״וַיַּעֲשׂוּ בְּנֵי הַגּוֹלָה הַשָּׁבִים מִן הַשְּׁבִי סוּכּוֹת וַיֵּשְׁבוּ בַסּוּכּוֹת כִּי לֹא עָשׂוּ מִימֵי יֵשׁוּעַ בִּן נוּן כֵּן בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְגוֹ׳ וַתְּהִי שִׂמְחָה גְּדוֹלָה מְאֹד״. אֶפְשָׁר בָּא דָּוִד וְלֹא עָשׂוּ סוּכּוֹת עַד שֶׁבָּא עֶזְרָא?

b10.he: אֶלָּא מַקִּישׁ בִּיאָתָם בִּימֵי עֶזְרָא לְבִיאָתָם בִּימֵי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, מָה בִּיאָתָם בִּימֵי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ מָנוּ שְׁמִיטִּין וְיוֹבְלוֹת וְקִדְּשׁוּ עָרֵי חוֹמָה, אַף בִּיאָתָן בִּימֵי עֶזְרָא מָנוּ שְׁמִיטִּין וְיוֹבְלוֹת וְקִדְּשׁוּ עָרֵי חוֹמָה.

b11.he: וְאוֹמֵר: ״וֶהֱבִיאֲךָ ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ אֶל הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר יָרְשׁוּ אֲבוֹתֶיךָ וִירִשְׁתָּהּ״, מַקִּישׁ יְרוּשָּׁתְךָ לִירוּשַּׁת אֲבוֹתֶיךָ — מָה יְרוּשַּׁת אֲבוֹתֶיךָ בְּחִידּוּשׁ כׇּל דְּבָרִים הַלָּלוּ, אַף יְרוּשָּׁתְךָ בְּחִידּוּשׁ כׇּל דְּבָרִים הַלָּלוּ.

b12.he: וְאִידַּךְ? דִּבְעוֹ רַחֲמֵי עַל יֵצֶר דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, וּבַטְּלֵיהּ, וְאַגֵּין זְכוּתָא עֲלַיְיהוּ כִּי סוּכָּה.

b13.he: וְהַיְינוּ דְּקָא קָפֵיד קְרָא עִילָּוֵיהּ דִּיהוֹשֻׁעַ, דִּבְכֹל דּוּכְתָּא כְּתִיב ״יְהוֹשֻׁעַ״, וְהָכָא כְּתִיב ״יֵשׁוּעַ״. בִּשְׁלָמָא מֹשֶׁה לָא בְּעָא רַחֲמֵי, דְּלָא הֲוָה זְכוּתָא דְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל, אֶלָּא יְהוֹשֻׁעַ דַּהֲוָה לֵיהּ זְכוּתָא דְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל, אַמַּאי לָא לִיבְעֵי רַחֲמֵי?

b14.he: וְהָא כְתִיב: ״אֲשֶׁר יָרְשׁוּ אֲבוֹתֶיךָ וִירִשְׁתָּהּ״! הָכִי קָאָמַר: כֵּיוָן דְּיָרְשׁוּ אֲבוֹתֶיךָ — יָרַשְׁתָּ אַתְּ.

b15.he: וּמִי מָנוּ שְׁמִיטִּין וְיוֹבְלוֹת? הַשְׁתָּא מִשֶּׁגָּלוּ שֵׁבֶט רְאוּבֵן וְשֵׁבֶט גָּד וַחֲצִי שֵׁבֶט מְנַשֶּׁה בָּטְלוּ יוֹבְלוֹת, עֶזְרָא דִּכְתִיב בֵּיהּ ״כׇּל הַקָּהָל כְּאֶחָד אַרְבַּע רִבּוֹא אַלְפַּיִם וְשֵׁשׁ מֵאוֹת וְשִׁשִּׁים״ הֲוָה מָנֵי?

b16.he: דְּתַנְיָא: מִשֶּׁגָּלוּ שֵׁבֶט רְאוּבֵן וְשֵׁבֶט גָד וַחֲצִי שֵׁבֶט הַמְנַשֶּׁה בָּטְלוּ יוֹבְלוֹת, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וּקְרָאתֶם דְּרוֹר בָּאָרֶץ לְכׇל יֹשְׁבֶיהָ״, בִּזְמַן שֶׁכֹּל יוֹשְׁבֶיהָ עָלֶיהָ, וְלֹא בִּזְמַן שֶׁגָּלוּ מִקְצָתָן.

b17.he: יָכוֹל הָיוּ עָלֶיהָ וְהֵן מְעוֹרָבִין, שֵׁבֶט בִּנְיָמִין בִּיהוּדָה וְשֵׁבֶט יְהוּדָה בְּבִנְיָמִין, יְהֵא יוֹבֵל נוֹהֵג? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״לְכׇל יֹשְׁבֶיהָ״ — בִּזְמַן שֶׁיּוֹשְׁבֶיהָ כְּתִיקּוּנָן, וְלֹא בִּזְמַן שֶׁהֵן מְעוֹרָבִין!

b18.he: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: מָנוּ יוֹבְלוֹת לְקַדֵּשׁ שְׁמִיטִּין.

messages.text: Continued from 31b: Rava inferred from Hillel’s ordinance that if a man says to his wife “This is your bill of divorce on the condition that you give me two hundred dinars,” she is divorced if she gave him the money with his consent, but not if she gave it against his will.

From the fact that it was necessary for Hillel to institute that giving against the will of the receiver is considered giving, in the case of houses of walled cities, one may infer that in general, giving against the will of the recipient is not considered giving.

notes.he: מדאיצטריך הלל לתקוני נתינה בעל כרחו [הוי נתינה הא בעלמא נתינה בע"כ] לא הויא נתינה - (פשיטא דאין לו לאדם לקבל מתנה בעל כרחו ולא הויא נתינה) וא"ת וכי איצטריך ליה להביא ראיה על זה דנתינה בעל כרחו לא הויא נתינה פשיטא דאין לו לאדם לקבל מתנה בעל כרחו ועוד היכי פליג על זה רב פפא וי"ל דודאי מתנה דרשות שאין לו שום צורך פשיטא דלא הויא בעל כרחו ורב פפא נמי לא פליג על זה אלא במתנה שיש בה צורך פליגי כמו הכא דאמר לה זה גיטך ע"מ שתתן לי מאתים זוז שהיא צריכה כדי לקיים תנאי הגט וכגון קבלה דמתני' [אבל] היכא דאיכא חובה לנותן כגון חוב או פקדון בהא ודאי הוי נתינה בעל כרחו כדאיתא פרק הגוזל בתרא (ב"ק קיח. ושם) הלוהו או שהפקיד אצלו בישוב לא יחזיר לו במדבר משמע הא בישוב מחזיר לו בעל כרחו ואם תאמר הא דתנן בפרק מי שאחזו (גיטין עד. ושם) הרי זה גיטך על מנת שתתן לי איצטליתי ואבדה איצטליתו רבן שמעון בן גמליאל אומר תתן דמיה והתם מיירי אפי' בעל כרחו דבעל מדפליגי רבנן עליה ואמרי איצטליתו דוקא קאמר תו בעי התם בגמרא האומר לאשה הרי זה גיטך ע"מ שתתני מאתים זוז וחזר ואמר לה מחולין לך מהו תיבעי לרבנן תיבעי לרשב"ג תיבעי לרבנן עד כאן לא קא אמרי רבנן התם אלא היכא דלא אחליה לגבה אבל הכא הא קאמר מחולין לך והא ע"כ דאמרי רבנן איצטליתו דוקא קאמר בעל כרחו מיירי דאי מדעתו לא גרע ממחולין לך ואפ"ה קאמר רשב"ג תתן לו דמיה אלמא סבירא ליה לרשב"ג דנתינה בעל כרחו הויא נתינה וא"כ היכי קאמר רבא הכא דלא הויא נתינה וצ"ל דלרבא מיירי התם דאמר רשב"ג תתן לו דמיה מדעתיה קאמר ואפילו הכי לרבנן איצטלית דוקא קאמר ואינה מגורשת והאי בעיא דהתם אינה אליבא דרבא דלרבא ודאי אליבא דרבנן אפילו מחולין לך לא מהני ואם תאמר לרבא דס"ל דאפילו בעיר לא הוי נתינה בע"כ א"כ למה היה ללוקח להטמין לימא לא מקבלינא ואז לא הוי נתינה והחליט לו אחר י"ב חדשים וי"ל דאם היה בעיר היה בוש ממנו אם לא היה מקבל וא"ת משמע דלרבא אפילו בפניו בע"כ לא הויא נתינה והיכי מצי להוכיח מהכא בפניו והלא תקנת הלל לא היתה כי אם שלא בפניו וכי איצטריך ליה להלל לתקוני שלא בפניו אבל בפניו בין מדעתו בין בעל כרחו הוי נתינה כדמתקיף ליה רב פפא וי"ל דמוכח הכי דאם איתא דבפניו הוי נתינה בעל כרחו לא הוה צריך להילל לתקוני שלא בפניו להיות חולש מעותיו ללשכה דהא אפשר לזכות לו ע"י אחר אלא שמע מינה מדאיצטריך ליה להלל לתקן נתינה בעל כרחו הא בעלמא כו' ורב פפא דאתקיף ליה לית ליה האי סברא:
notes.en: In brief: Tosafot ask: why would one need a proof that giving against the recipient’s will is not giving? It is obvious that a person need not accept a gift against his will; and how, then, could Rav Pappa disagree? They answer: a voluntary gift that the giver has no need to give is certainly not giving against the recipient’s will, and Rav Pappa does not disagree about that. They disagree only about a gift that the giver needs to give, as here, where he said “This is your bill of divorce on the condition that you give me two hundred zuz,” and she needs to give in order to fulfill the condition of the bill of divorce; and as with the payment in our mishna. But where the giver is obligated, as with a debt or a deposit, giving against the recipient’s will is certainly giving, as in Bava Kamma (118a): one who lent to another or deposited with him in a settled place may not return it to him in the desert, which implies that in a settled place he returns it to him even against his will. They ask further from Gittin (74a): “This is your bill of divorce on the condition that you give me my cloak,” and the cloak was lost: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says she gives its value. From the dilemma in the Gemara there (where the husband said “the two hundred zuz are forgiven to you”) Tosafot show that the case speaks of payment against the husband’s will, so Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel holds that giving against his will is giving; how then can Rava say here that it is not? They answer that according to Rava, Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel speaks there of payment with the husband’s consent, and the dilemma there is not according to Rava, for whom, according to the Rabbis, even “they are forgiven to you” does not help. They ask: according to Rava, who holds that even in the city giving against the recipient’s will is not giving, why did the buyer need to hide? Let him say “I do not accept,” and it is not giving, and the house becomes his after twelve months. They answer: had he been in the city, he would have been ashamed not to accept. Last, it is implied that according to Rava even in his presence giving against his will is not giving; how can he prove this from Hillel’s ordinance, which was made only for payment not in the buyer’s presence, as Rav Pappa objects? They answer: if giving in his presence against his will were giving, Hillel would not have needed to institute, for a case not in his presence, that the seller place his money in the chamber, since it could be acquired on the buyer’s behalf through another person; rather, from the fact that Hillel needed to institute that giving against his will is giving, conclude that in general it is not. Rav Pappa, who objects, does not hold this reasoning. Open on Sefaria for the full text.

messages.text: But perhaps when it was necessary for Hillel to institute this ordinance, it was specifically for a case where the seller gives the money not in the presence of the buyer; but if he repays the buyer in his presence, then whether the buyer was repaid with his consent or whether it was against his will, it is considered a valid act of giving.
messages.lead: Rav Pappa objects to this, and some say it was Rav Ashi who objected:

notes.he: כגון זה שהיה נטמן ומשום דתרתי לריעותא איכא דשלא בפניו הוא ובעל כרחו הוא משום הכי איצטריך ליה להלל לתקוני:
notes.en: Not in his presence: like this one, who was hiding. And because there are two drawbacks, that it is not in his presence and that it is against his will, for that reason Hillel needed to institute [the ordinance].

notes.he: ומש"ה איצטריך ליה לתקוני נתינה שלא בפניו כגון זה [שחולש מעותיו בלשכה:
notes.en: And therefore he needed to institute giving not in his presence, as with this one [who places his money in the chamber].

messages.text: One may infer from the ordinance of Hillel that if one says to his wife: This is your bill of divorce on the condition that you will give me two hundred dinars, and she gave it to him, whether it was with his consent or whether it was against his will, it is a valid act of giving.
messages.lead: There are those who say an opposite version of this discussion:

messages.text: And this is because when it was necessary for Hillel to institute this ordinance, it was specifically for a case where the seller gives the money not in the presence of the buyer. But if the seller repays him in his presence, whether the buyer was repaid with his consent or whether it was against his will, it is considered a valid act of giving.

But perhaps, whether she gives him the money in his presence or not in his presence, if she gives it with his consent, yes, it is valid, but if she gives it against his will, it is not considered a valid act of giving.
messages.lead: Rav Pappa objects to this, and some say it was Rav Shimi bar Ashi who objected:

messages.text: And Hillel instituted what was necessary, to remedy the practical occurrence that buyers would hide themselves at the end of the year. But even if the seller finds the buyer and the buyer refuses to accept payment, it would be necessary for Hillel to institute an ordinance.

notes.he: ואי הוי נמי לוקח התם ולא הוה בעי לקבולינהו הוה איצטריך להלל לתקוני דבעל כרחו תיהוי נתינה:
notes.en: [Hillel] instituted what was needed: and even if the buyer had been there and had not wanted to accept [the money], Hillel would have needed to institute that [giving] against his will is giving.

notes.he: הא בעלמא בין בפניו ובין שלא בפניו מדעתו אין בעל כרחו לא]:
notes.en: And Hillel instituted what he needed. But in general, whether in his presence or not in his presence: with his consent, yes; against his will, no.

messages.text: Mishna
The halakhic status of any area that is located within the city wall is like that of the houses of walled cities in terms of its redemption, except for the fields located therein.

notes.he: כל שהוא לפנים מן החומה כגון בתי [בדים] ובתי מרחצאות ומגדלים ושובכים וכל כיוצא בהן הרי הן כבתי ערי חומה ונחלטין עמה לאחר י"ב חדש:
notes.en: Anything within the wall, such as olive-press houses, bathhouses, towers, dovecotes and everything like them: these are like the houses of walled cities and are transferred in perpetuity along with it after twelve months.

notes.he: שאם יש שדות [בתוך] העיר אין נחלטין:
notes.en: Except for the fields: for if there are fields within the city, they are not transferred in perpetuity.

messages.text: Even the fields are included in this category.
With regard to a house that is built in the wall itself:
Its halakhic status is not like that of the houses of walled cities.
The outer wall of the house is considered the city wall, and therefore it has the status of a house in a walled city.
Gemara

The verse states: “Then the house that is in the walled city shall stand in possession of the one who bought it in perpetuity” (Leviticus 25:30). I have derived only that this is the halakha with regard to a house; from where is it derived to include olive presses, bathhouses, towers, dovecotes, pits, ditches, and caves? The verse states: “That is in the walled city,” indicating that anything situated within the city is included.

verse.he: וְאִם לֹא־יִגָּאֵל עַד־מְלֹאת לוֹ שָׁנָה תְמִימָה וְקָם הַבַּיִת אֲשֶׁר־בָּעִיר אֲשֶׁר־[לוֹ] (לא) חֹמָה לַצְּמִיתֻת לַקֹּנֶה אֹתוֹ לְדֹרֹתָיו לֹא יֵצֵא בַּיֹּבֵל׃
verse.en: If it is not redeemed before a full year has elapsed, the house in the walled city shall pass to the purchaser beyond reclaim throughout the ages; it shall not be released in the jubilee.

notes.he: וקם הבית אשר בעיר (ויקרא כ״ה:ל׳):
notes.en: Gemara. House: “then the house that is in the city shall stand” (Leviticus 25:30).

notes.he: משטיי"ר וקבועה בקרקע:
notes.en: Towers: (Rashi adds an Old French gloss), and fixed in the ground.

notes.he: דכתיב וקם הבית אשר בעיר אשר לו:
notes.en: House: as it is written: “Then the house that is in the city that has [a wall] shall stand.”

notes.he: שהוא בית דירה שנחלט:
notes.en: Only a house: which is a dwelling house, which is transferred in perpetuity.

messages.text: If so, one might have thought that I should include even the fields that are inside the city. Therefore, the verse states: “House,” which excludes a field; it does not resemble a house in any way, since it does not contain any items. This is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.

notes.he: והני דלעיל דמו לבית:
notes.en: The verse states “house”: and those listed above resemble a house.

notes.he: דדמי לבית למעוטי שדות דברי ר' יהודה:
notes.en: The verse states “house”: what resembles a house, to exclude fields. These are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

messages.text: The verse states: “House.” I have derived only a house; from where is it derived to include olive presses, bathhouses, towers, dovecotes, pits, ditches, and caves, and even fields? The verse states: “That is in the walled city,” to include anything inside the city.
But isn’t it written: “House”? If Rabbi Meir includes even a field, what is excluded by the word “house”?

notes.he: לר' מאיר הא כתיב בית דמשמע מידי דדמי לבית נחלט ולא שדה:
notes.en: But [according to] Rabbi Meir, isn’t “house” written, which implies that what resembles a house is transferred in perpetuity, but not a field?

messages.text: Actually, everyone agrees that the term “house” serves to exclude a field. The difference of opinion between Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda is with regard to a quarry and a sand bed. According to Rabbi Meir, such areas are considered similar to houses and are therefore included in the halakha.

notes.he: מקום שאינו ראוי לזריעה איכא בינייהו דשדות ממש לא קאמר רבי מאיר דהא בית כתיב ביה אלא חולסית ומצולה קמרבי דדמו לבית דלאו בני זריעה נינהו וראויין לבנין בית חולסית ליטול משם אבנים ומצולה ליטול מהן חול ורבי יהודה סבר כשדות דמו:
notes.en: A quarry: the difference between them is a place that is not fit for sowing. For Rabbi Meir does not mean actual fields, since “house” is written there; rather, he includes a quarry and a sand bed, which resemble a house, since they are not fit for sowing and are suited to building a house: a quarry, to take stones from there, and a sand bed, to take sand from it. And Rabbi Yehuda holds that they resemble fields.

notes.he: פירש"י ליטול משם אבנים ומצולה ליטול משם חול ורשב"ם פירש בב"ב (דף סז. ושם) חולסית ליטול הימנה זכוכית ומצולה כמו (ברכות דף ט:) מצולה של דגים:
notes.en: A quarry: Rashi explains: to take stones from there, and a sand bed, to take sand from there. And the Rashbam explained in Bava Batra (67a): ḥolasit, to take glass from it; and metzula, as in “a metzula of fish” (Berakhot 9b) [a deep pool].

notes.he: סלעים:
notes.en: Ḥolasit: rocks.

notes.he: עומקה בעלמא שיש בה מים שאינן ראוין לזריעה ואינן דומין כ"כ לבית דירה. לר' יהודה דממעט שדות ממעט נמי הני דדמו לשדה דלית בהו דירה לר' מאיר דבעי לרבויי אפי' שדות שדות גמורין לא מצי לרבויי משום דכתיב בית אבל חולסית ומצולה דדמו לבית למגדל ובור הכי נמי דסבר דנחלטין עמה]:
notes.en: And metzula: simply a deep place that has water. These are not fit for sowing, and they do not so much resemble a dwelling house. According to Rabbi Yehuda, who excludes fields, he also excludes these, which resemble a field, since there is no dwelling in them. According to Rabbi Meir, who wants to include even fields, he cannot include actual fields, because “house” is written; but a quarry and a sand bed, which resemble a house, like a tower and a pit, he indeed holds are transferred in perpetuity along with it.

messages.text: With regard to a quarry and a sand bed inside the walls of a city, Rabbi Meir says: They are considered like houses, and Rabbi Yehuda says: They are considered like fields.

notes.he: בניחותא:
notes.en: And it is taught: [said] as a support [not as a challenge].

notes.he: סיועא:
notes.en: And it is taught: a support.

messages.text: § The mishna teaches: With regard to a house that is built in the wall itself, Rabbi Yehuda says: Its halakhic status is not like that of the houses of walled cities, and Rabbi Shimon says: The outer wall of the house is considered the city wall.
messages.quote: a house that is built in the wall

notes.he: ר' יהודה אומר אינו נחלט כבתי ערי חומה לפי שהוא דומה כאילו עומד חוץ לעיר:
notes.en: A house built into the city wall: Rabbi Yehuda says it is not transferred in perpetuity like the houses of walled cities, because it is as though it stands outside the city.

notes.he: של בית הוא חומתו ודומה כמגדל שעומד בחומה (ולהלאה) [ונחלט:
notes.en: Rabbi Shimon says: the outer wall of the house is its wall, and it is like a tower that stands in the wall, and it is transferred in perpetuity.

messages.text: And both of them derived their opinions from one verse: “Then she let them down by a cord through the window; for her house was upon the side of the wall; and she dwelt upon the wall” (Joshua 2:15).

verse.he: וַתּוֹרִדֵם בַּחֶבֶל בְּעַד הַחַלּוֹן כִּי בֵיתָהּ בְּקִיר הַחוֹמָה וּבַחוֹמָה הִיא יוֹשָׁבֶת׃
verse.en: She let them down by a rope through the window—for her dwelling was at the outer side of the city wall and she lived in the actual wall.

messages.text: Rabbi Shimon holds that the last phrase should be understood in accordance with the simple meaning of the verse, that her house was attached to the outer wall and it was considered inside the walled city; and Rabbi Yehuda holds that “she dwelt upon the wall” means she was a resident of the wall itself, but not a resident of the city enclosed within the wall.

notes.he: דחזינן דביתה בתוך החומה וקאמר בחומה היא יושבת כלומר בעיר חומה היא יושבת:
notes.en: In accordance with the simple meaning of the verse: for we see that her house was within the wall, and it says “and she dwelt upon the wall,” that is to say, she dwelt in a walled city.

notes.he: כמו שהוא משמע כי ביתה בקיר החומה ואפי' הכי ובחומה היא יושבת פי' לפנים מן החומה:
notes.en: Rabbi Shimon holds in accordance with the simple meaning of the verse: as it implies, “for her house was upon the side of the wall,” and even so, “and she dwelt upon the wall,” meaning within the wall.

notes.dh: ור' יהודה סבר בחומה היא יושבת
notes.he: (אי' דאמר שגגותיה היא יושבת) כתיב ולא בעיר חומה כלומר אינו כלפנים מן החומה]:
notes.en: And Rabbi Yehuda holds: “she dwelt upon the wall” is written, and not in a walled city; that is to say, it is not like [a house] within the wall. [A parenthetical in the text reads: some say, she dwelt on its roofs.]

messages.caption: Inside the city wall: what Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Meir count as houses of a walled city, and the house built into the wall.

messages.text: Mishna

The halakhic status of a house in a city whose houses are attached and their rooftops constitute the top of its wall, and likewise, the status of a house in a city that is not surrounded by a wall from the era of Joshua, son of Nun, even if a surrounding wall was constructed during a later period, is not like that of the houses of walled cities.

notes.he: שלא הקיפוה חומה אלא הקיפוה בבתים ותכופות הבתים זו לזו כחומה:
notes.en: Mishna. Whose roofs are its wall: they did not surround it with a wall, but surrounded it with houses, and the houses are pressed one against another like a wall.

notes.he: איכא דאמרי שכל החומה סביב מלאה גגות ואיכא דאמרי שגגותיה משופעין עד הארץ והן הן החומות:
notes.en: A city whose roofs are its walls: some say that the whole wall around is full of roofs, and some say that its roofs slope down to the ground, and they are the walls.

messages.text: And these are the houses of walled cities: Any city in which there are at least three courtyards, each containing two houses, and which is surrounded by a wall from the era of Joshua, son of Nun,

notes.he: שבכל אחת ואחת שני בתים מיקריא עיר:
notes.en: Three courtyards: [a place with three courtyards,] in each of which there are two houses, is called a city.

messages.text: e.g., the ancient fort [katzra] of Tzippori, and the fortress [ḥakra] of Gush Ḥalav, and ancient Yodfat, and Gamla, and Gedod, and Ḥadid, and Ono, and Jerusalem, and likewise other similar cities.

notes.he: שם עיר קטנה שמחוץ לציפורי:
notes.en: Katzra: the name of a small city outside Tzippori.

messages.text: Gemara

With regard to the statement of the mishna that the halakhic status of a house in a city whose rooftops constitute the top of its wall is not like that of the houses of walled cities, the Sages taught:
messages.quote: a city whose rooftops constitute its wall

messages.text: When the verse states: “The house that is in the city that has a wall” (Leviticus 25:30), this is referring specifically to a city that has an actual wall and not merely a wall of roofs.

verse.he: וְאִם לֹא־יִגָּאֵל עַד־מְלֹאת לוֹ שָׁנָה תְמִימָה וְקָם הַבַּיִת אֲשֶׁר־בָּעִיר אֲשֶׁר־[לוֹ] (לא) חֹמָה לַצְּמִיתֻת לַקֹּנֶה אֹתוֹ לְדֹרֹתָיו לֹא יֵצֵא בַּיֹּבֵל׃
verse.en: If it is not redeemed before a full year has elapsed, the house in the walled city shall pass to the purchaser beyond reclaim throughout the ages; it shall not be released in the jubilee.

notes.he: שגגותיה חומתה:
notes.en: Gemara. Shur iggar [a wall of roofs]: [a city] whose roofs are its wall.

notes.he: דכתיב] אשר לו חומה סביב. חומה [ממש] סביב לעיר בעינן. ולא שור איגר. חומה של גגות:
notes.en: Wall: as it is written, “that has a wall around.” We require [an actual] wall around the city, and not a shur iggar, a wall of roofs.

messages.text: When the next verse states: “But the houses of the villages that have no wall round about them shall be reckoned with the fields of the country,” this serves to exclude Tiberias from being considered a walled city, as the sea is its wall on one side and it is not fully encircled by a physical wall.

verse.he: וּבָתֵּי הַחֲצֵרִים אֲשֶׁר אֵין־לָהֶם חֹמָה סָבִיב עַל־שְׂדֵה הָאָרֶץ יֵחָשֵׁב גְּאֻלָּה תִּהְיֶה־לּוֹ וּבַיֹּבֵל יֵצֵא׃
verse.en: But houses in villages that have no encircling walls shall be classed as open country: they may be redeemed, and they shall be released through the jubilee.

notes.he: דכתיב ובתי החצרים אשר אין להם חומה סביב מכלל דבתי ערי חומה צריכין חומה סביב:
notes.en: Around: as it is written: “But the houses of the villages that have no wall around them.” By inference, the houses of walled cities require a wall all around.

messages.alt: named here Rabbi Eliezer bar Yosei
messages.text: Since the verse states: “Which has [lo] a wall,” with lo written with an alef, according to which the verse may also be taken to mean: Which does not have a wall, this indicates that even if a city does not have a wall now, but it had a wall before, in the era of Joshua, son of Nun, it retains its status as a walled city.

verse.he: וְאִם לֹא־יִגָּאֵל עַד־מְלֹאת לוֹ שָׁנָה תְמִימָה וְקָם הַבַּיִת אֲשֶׁר־בָּעִיר אֲשֶׁר־[לוֹ] (לא) חֹמָה לַצְּמִיתֻת לַקֹּנֶה אֹתוֹ לְדֹרֹתָיו לֹא יֵצֵא בַּיֹּבֵל׃
verse.en: If it is not redeemed before a full year has elapsed, the house in the walled city shall pass to the purchaser beyond reclaim throughout the ages; it shall not be released in the jubilee.

notes.he: לוא כתיב משמע לא ומשמע לו כלומר אין לו עכשיו והיה לו חומה קודם הוה נמי בית חלוט בהו:
notes.en: Lo a wall: lo is written [lamed-vav-alef]; it implies lo, “not,” and it implies lo, “to it.” That is to say, it does not have [a wall] now but it had a wall before; [a house in it,] too, is transferred in perpetuity.

notes.he: פירש רש"י לוא כתיב משמע לו ומשמע לא כלומר אין לו עכשיו והיה לו קודם לכן ואינו כן בחומשין מדויקות כתיב [לא באל"ף וקרי בוי"ו] (בוי"ו ולא קרי באל"ף):
notes.en: Which has a wall: Rashi explains that lo is written [lamed-vav-alef], implying “to it” and implying “not”; that is, it does not have [a wall] now but it had one before. But it is not so: in precise Ḥumashim it is written lo with an alef, and read with a vav. [Another printed reading has: with a vav, and not read with an alef.]

notes.he: באלף כתיב כלומר אע"פ שאין לו עכשיו והיה לו קודם לכן נידון כבתי ערי חומה:
notes.en: Which has [lo] a wall: it is written with an alef; that is to say, even though it does not have [a wall] now, if it had one before, it is judged like the houses of walled cities.

messages.text: The daf names this Tanna Rabbi Eliezer bar Yosei here; on 32b the Gemara quotes the same words in the name of Rabbi Elazar bar Yosei.

§ The mishna teaches: And these are the houses of walled cities: The ancient fort of Tzippori, and the fortress of Gush Ḥalav, and ancient Yodfat, and Gamla, and Gedod, and Ḥadid, and Ono, and Jerusalem, and likewise other similar cities. The Sages taught in a baraita:
messages.quote: the ancient fort of Tzippori, and the fortress of Gush Ḥalav, and ancient Yodfat

notes.he: [קצרה הישנה שבתחום ציפורי]:
notes.en: Old Katzra, which is within the boundary of Tzippori.

messages.text: Gamla is in the Galilee, and Gedod is in Transjordan, and Ḥadid and Ono and Jerusalem are in Judea.
What is the tanna of this baraita saying? Are these the only walled cities in the Galilee, Transjordan, and Judea?
messages.quote: Gamla is in the Galilee, and Gedod is in Transjordan

notes.he: וכי אין עיר מוקפת חומה בגליל אלא גמלא ובעבר הירדן אלא גדוד:
notes.en: What is he saying: is there no city surrounded by a wall in the Galilee except Gamla, and in Transjordan except Gedod?

notes.he: וכי אין עיר מוקפת חומה בגליל אלא גמלא ובעבר הירדן אלא גדוד ואם תאמר אמאי לא פריך כמו כן אמתני' ויש לומר דפריך שפיר אברייתא לפי שדקדקה יותר דמפרשא בהדיא גמלא בגליל וגדוד בעבר הירדן:
notes.en: What is he saying: is there no city surrounded by a wall in the Galilee except Gamla, and in Transjordan except Gedod? And if you say: why does he not ask the same of the mishna? One can say that he rightly asks it of the baraita, because it is more precise, stating explicitly Gamla in the Galilee and Gedod in Transjordan.

messages.text: This is what the baraita is saying: Until Gamla in the Galilee, i.e., all towns in the Galilee from Gamla southward were surrounded by a wall from the era of Joshua, son of Nun; and likewise, all towns until Gedod in Transjordan, which is the easternmost city, were surrounded by a wall; and Ḥadid and Ono and Jerusalem in Judea were surrounded by a wall from the era of Joshua, son of Nun.

notes.he: כל עיירות שבגליל עד גמלא היו מוקפות חומה מימות יהושע:
notes.en: Until Gamla: all the towns in the Galilee as far as Gamla were surrounded by a wall from the days of Joshua.

notes.he: כלומר כל העיירות שבגליל שיתירות מגמלא ועד גמלא בכלל שגמלא היו בה ג' חצרות של [ב'] ב' בתים והן מוקפין חומה מימות יהושע בן נון נידונין כבתי ערי חומה למעוטי הקטנות מגמלא [שאין נידונין] וכן עד גדוד בעבר הירדן וחדיד ואונו וירושלים ביהודה שכל אותן שהן גדולות כיוצא בהן או יתירות מהן ומוקפות חומה מימות יהושע בן נון נדונין (כערי) [כבתי] ערי חומה. [רבא אמר. הא דתנא גמלא בגליל לאפוקי גמלא שיש בשאר ארצות שאינן מוקפות מימות יהושע ואף לא גדוד דשאר ארצות. והנך קצרה וחקרה ויודפת דמוקפות חומה מימות יהושע דלא איכא דכוותיה בשאר ארצות שיהא להן שמות הללו ואין מוקפות חומה לא איצטריך ליה לאדכורי בתוספת':
notes.en: Until Gamla in the Galilee: that is to say, all the towns in the Galilee that are larger than Gamla, up to and including Gamla (for Gamla had three courtyards of two houses each), and that are surrounded by a wall from the days of Joshua son of Nun, are judged like the houses of walled cities; to exclude those smaller than Gamla, [which are not so judged]. And likewise until Gedod in Transjordan; and Ḥadid and Ono and Jerusalem in Judea: all those as large as them or larger, and surrounded by a wall from the days of Joshua son of Nun, are judged like the houses of walled cities. Rava said: when the baraita teaches “Gamla in the Galilee,” it is to exclude a Gamla in other lands, which is not surrounded [by a wall] from the days of Joshua; and likewise not Gedod of other lands. And those others, Katzra, Ḥakra and Yodfat, which are surrounded by a wall from the days of Joshua: since there are none like them in other lands bearing these names and not surrounded by a wall, he did not need to mention them in the Tosefta [the baraita].

messages.text: The baraita is elucidating the mishna, which mentions these cities. The baraita is teaching that the Gamla referred to in the mishna is the one in the Galilee, to the exclusion of any Gamla found in other lands, i.e., Judea and Transjordan. Likewise, Gedod is the one in Transjordan, to the exclusion of Gedod in other lands, Judea and the Galilee. In the same vein, Ḥadid, Ono, and Jerusalem are specifically the cities in Judea known by those names.

notes.he: האי תנא אתא לפרושי מתני' והכי קאמר גמלא דקתני מתני' דהוות מוקפת חומה מימות יהושע היינו גמלא דגליל:
notes.en: Rava said: this tanna comes to explain our mishna, and this is what he says: the Gamla that our mishna teaches was surrounded by a wall from the days of Joshua is the Gamla of the Galilee.

notes.he: דאי איכא גמלא בעבר הירדן וביהודה לא הויא מוקפת חומה מימות יהושע וכן גדוד וכן חדיד וירושלים ביהודה לאפוקי עיירות שבגליל ועבר הירדן שנקראו חדיד ואונו וירושלים אינן מוקפות מימות יהושע:
notes.en: To exclude: that if there is a Gamla in Transjordan or in Judea, it was not surrounded by a wall from the days of Joshua. And likewise Gedod. And likewise Ḥadid and Jerusalem in Judea: to exclude towns in the Galilee and in Transjordan called Ḥadid, Ono and Jerusalem, which are not surrounded by a wall from the days of Joshua.

messages.text: With regard to those other cities mentioned in the mishna, e.g., Yodfat, since there are no cities in other lands with similar names, it was not necessary for the tanna of the baraita to state them.

notes.he: אינך דקא חשיב במתני' כגון קצרה ויודפת דליכא בדוכתא אחריתי דמסקי כשמתייהו לא איצטריך למיתני ברייתא בהי ארעא קיימי:
notes.en: Those that have none like them: those that [the tanna] counts in our mishna, such as Katzra and Yodfat, which have no namesakes elsewhere; the baraita did not need to teach in which land they stand.

messages.text: And is ownership of a house in Jerusalem transferred in perpetuity to the buyer after one year, in the manner of houses of walled cities? But isn’t it taught in a baraita:
Ten matters were stated with regard to Jerusalem, one of which is that ownership of a house situated in Jerusalem is not transferred in perpetuity one year after its sale.

notes.he: מפרש בב"ק בפרק מרובה (בבא קמא דף פב:) וזה אחד מהם:
notes.en: Ten matters: they are explained in Bava Kamma, in chapter Merubeh (Bava Kamma 82b), and this is one of them.

notes.he: משום דכתיב (ויקרא כה) לקונה אותו לדורותיו וקסבר לא נתחלקה ירושלים לשבטים ומאן קא מקני ליה:
notes.en: A house is not transferred in perpetuity: because it is written (Leviticus 25:30) “to the one who bought it, throughout his generations,” and he holds that Jerusalem was not divided among the tribes; so who would transfer it to him?

notes.he: פרטן בפרק מרובה:
notes.en: Ten matters were stated with regard to Jerusalem: they are detailed in chapter Merubeh [Bava Kamma 82b].

messages.text: The tanna means that ownership of a house may be transferred in perpetuity in any city that is like Jerusalem, i.e., which is surrounded by a wall from the era of Joshua, son of Nun, but the halakha with regard to such a city is not like Jerusalem itself, since while with regard to Jerusalem, ownership of a house inside it is not transferred in perpetuity, here, with regard to cities similar to Jerusalem, a house in them may be transferred in perpetuity to the buyer.

notes.he: כלומר כעין ירושלים בעינן שיהא מוקפת חומה מימות יהושע ולא כירושלים עצמה דאין הבית חלוט בה שהיא של כל ישראל:
notes.en: Rabbi Yoḥanan said: like Jerusalem: that is to say, we require [a city] like Jerusalem, that it be surrounded by a wall from the days of Joshua son of Nun; but not like Jerusalem itself, in which a house is not transferred in perpetuity, since it belongs to all Israel.

notes.he: גבי אלו מקומות שהזכרנו:
notes.en: While here: with regard to these places that we mentioned.

messages.text: Didn’t Rav Yosef say in resolution of another difficulty: There were two places called Kadesh? Here, too, one can say that there were two places called Jerusalem in Judea, and the mishna is referring to the one where ownership of houses transfers in perpetuity.

notes.dh: לאו מי אמר רב יוסף וכו'
notes.he: במס' מכות בפ' אלו הן הגולין (מכות דף י.):
notes.en: Didn’t Rav Yosef say, and so on: in tractate Makkot, in chapter Elu Hen HaGolin (Makkot 10a).

notes.he: ותימה דלרבא נמי אנו צריכין לומר כן דתרי ירושלים הוו וי"ל דלרבא אין אנו צריכין לומר ביהודה תרי ירושלים הוו אלא בשאר ארצות אבל לרב אשי צ"ל ביהודה תרי ירושלים הוו:
notes.en: Here too there were two Jerusalems: and it is puzzling, for according to Rava too we need to say this, that there were two Jerusalems. One can say that according to Rava we need not say that there were two Jerusalems in Judea, only in other lands; but according to Rav Ashi we must say that there were two Jerusalems in Judea.

notes.he: (קאמר) במסכת מכות בפרק אלו הן הגולין:
notes.en: There were two [places called] Kadesh: in tractate Makkot, in chapter Elu Hen HaGolin.

messages.text: Why did the Sages count specifically these cities as those walled since the days of Joshua, son of Nun? They counted them because when the exiles ascended to Eretz Yisrael from Babylonia, they discovered these cities and sanctified them; but the sanctity of the first walled cities was nullified when the sanctity of the land was nullified and the Jewish people were exiled.
messages.lead: With regard to the cities listed in the mishna, it is taught in a baraita:

notes.he: המנויות במשנתינו:
notes.en: These: those enumerated in our mishna.

notes.he: מפרש במסכת שבועות (דף טז.) דמקדשי לה בשתי תודות ובשיר ובית דין מהלכין ושתי תודות אחריהן וכו':
notes.en: And they sanctified them: it is explained in tractate Shevuot (16a) that one sanctifies it with two thanksgiving offerings and with song, and the court walks, with the two thanksgiving offerings behind them, and so on.

notes.he: שאין קדושת הארץ נוהגת בהן ואין בהן דין ערי חומה:
notes.en: Were nullified: for the sanctity of the land does not apply in them, and the law of walled cities does not apply in them.

notes.he: בחורבן ראשון:
notes.en: When the sanctity of the land was nullified: at the first destruction.

notes.he: יודפת וגמלא כו']:
notes.en: Why did the Sages count these: Yodfat and Gamla, and so on.

notes.he: וקידשום לשמיטה ויובלות ולמעשרות (ולתודות) [ולתורת] בתי ערי חומה:
notes.en: And they sanctified them for the Sabbatical Year and the Jubilees, for tithes, and for the law of the houses of walled cities.

notes.he: שהיו קדושות כבר והן מוקפות חומה מימות יהושע בטלה קדושתן משבטלה הארץ משגלו]:
notes.en: But the first ones: which had already been sanctified and were surrounded by a wall from the days of Joshua, their sanctity was nullified when the [sanctity of the] land was nullified, when they were exiled.

messages.text: Apparently, Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yosei, holds that the initial consecration of Eretz Yisrael in the days of Joshua consecrated it for its time, until the exile, but did not consecrate Eretz Yisrael forever.

notes.he: שקידשה יהושע:
notes.en: The first consecration: with which Joshua sanctified it.

notes.he: שקידשם יהושע:
notes.en: Since he says “they sanctified them,” he holds that the first consecration: [that is,] with which Joshua sanctified them.

notes.he: כל זמן שהיו בה עד (שגלו) [שעת החורבן]:
notes.en: Sanctified it for its time: all the time that they were in it, until [the time of the destruction].

notes.he: שאין אותה [קדושה] נוהגת כשחזרו מן הגולה:
notes.en: And did not sanctify it for the future: that [sanctity] does not apply when they returned from the exile.

messages.text: But raise a contradiction from another baraita:

And were these cities enumerated in the mishna the only walled cities from the days of Joshua? But isn’t it already stated: “There was not a city that we took not from them; sixty cities, all the region of Argob…all these cities were fortified with high walls, gates, and bars” (Deuteronomy 3:4–5)?

verse.he: וַנִּלְכֹּד אֶת־כׇּל־עָרָיו בָּעֵת הַהִוא לֹא הָיְתָה קִרְיָה אֲשֶׁר לֹא־לָקַחְנוּ מֵאִתָּם שִׁשִּׁים עִיר כׇּל־חֶבֶל אַרְגֹּב מַמְלֶכֶת עוֹג בַּבָּשָׁן׃ כׇּל־אֵלֶּה עָרִים בְּצֻרֹת חוֹמָה גְבֹהָה דְּלָתַיִם וּבְרִיחַ לְבַד מֵעָרֵי הַפְּרָזִי הַרְבֵּה מְאֹד׃
verse.en: At that time we captured all his towns; there was not a town that we did not take from them: sixty towns, the whole district of Argob, the kingdom of Og in Bashan— all those towns were fortified with high walls, gates, and bars—apart from a great number of unwalled towns.

notes.he: שהוזכרו למעלה היו מוקפות חומה מימות יהושע והלא כבר [נאמר ששים עיר וגו' וכתיב כל אלה חומה גבוהה]:
notes.en: And were these alone, mentioned above, surrounded by a wall from the days of Joshua? But it is already [stated: “sixty cities,” and so on, and it is written: “all these were fortified with high walls”].

messages.text: Rather, why did the Sages specifically count these cities? They counted them because when the exiles ascended from Babylonia they discovered these and sanctified them.

Can the baraita really mean that they sanctified them? But we say later in the same baraita that it is not necessary to sanctify them. Rather, the baraita means that they found these cities and counted them in the mishna.

notes.he: לקמן בסוף דהא מילתא דלא צריכי לקדושי דקתני סיפא ולא אלו בלבד אלא כל שתעלה בידך כו' שקידשה לשעתה ולעתיד לבא:
notes.en: But you say: below, at the end, that this is a matter that does not need to be sanctified, as it teaches in the latter clause: “And not only these, but any that comes into your hand, and so on,” for it sanctified it for its time and for the future.

notes.dh: הא אמרי' (השתא) לקמן דלא צריך לקדושינהו
notes.he: כדקאמר מפני שקדושה הראשונה קידשה לשעתה וקידשה לעתיד לבוא:
notes.en: But we say below that there is no need to sanctify them: as it says, because the first consecration sanctified it for its time and sanctified it for the future.

notes.he: אלא מצאו אלו שלא נשתנו מכמות שהיו [ומנאום להילכותיהן]:
notes.en: Rather, they found these, which had not changed from what they had been, [and counted them for their halakhot].

messages.text: And not only these; rather, with regard to any city for which you receive a tradition from your ancestors that it is surrounded by a wall from the days of Joshua, son of Nun, all these mitzvot of walled cities are observed in it, due to the fact that the initial consecration of Eretz Yisrael consecrated it for its time and consecrated it forever.

notes.he: שנוהגות בעיירו' שמוקפות חומה [מימות יהושע] נוהגות בהן. כדתנן בטהרות עיירות המוקפות חומה מימות יהושע בן נון מקודשות ממנה:
notes.en: All these mitzvot: that apply in towns surrounded by a wall [from the days of Joshua] apply in them, as we learned in [the order of] Tohorot: “Towns surrounded by a wall from the days of Joshua son of Nun are holier than it [the rest of the land].”

messages.text: Evidently, Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yosei, holds that the initial consecration of Eretz Yisrael is eternal.

If you wish, say that this is a dispute between two tanna’im, and they disagree with regard to the opinion of Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yosei. And if you wish, say instead that one of the baraitot, specifically the second one, was actually said by Rabbi Elazar bar Yosei. As it is taught in a baraita:

notes.he: הך דקתני קידשה לעתיד לבא ר' אלעזר בר יוסי אמרה כי היכי דקאמר אע"פ שאין לו עכשיו ואע"ג דחרוב לא בטלה קדושתיה:
notes.en: One of them: this one, which teaches that it sanctified it for the future, Rabbi Elazar bar Yosei said it, just as he says “even though it does not have [a wall] now”: although it is destroyed, its sanctity is not nullified.

notes.dh: [תרי תנאי ואליבא דר' ישמעאל בר' יוסי
notes.he: מר אמר קידשה לעתיד לבוא ומר אמר לא קידשה]:
notes.en: Two tannaim, and according to Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosei: one says it sanctified for the future, and one says it did not sanctify.

messages.text: Since the verse states: “Which has [lo] a wall,” with lo written with an alef, according to which the verse may also be taken to mean: Which does not have a wall, this indicates that even if a city does not have a wall now, but it had a wall before, in the era of Joshua, son of Nun, it retains its status as a walled city.

verse.he: וְאִם לֹא־יִגָּאֵל עַד־מְלֹאת לוֹ שָׁנָה תְמִימָה וְקָם הַבַּיִת אֲשֶׁר־בָּעִיר אֲשֶׁר־[לוֹ] (לא) חֹמָה לַצְּמִיתֻת לַקֹּנֶה אֹתוֹ לְדֹרֹתָיו לֹא יֵצֵא בַּיֹּבֵל׃
verse.en: If it is not redeemed before a full year has elapsed, the house in the walled city shall pass to the purchaser beyond reclaim throughout the ages; it shall not be released in the jubilee.

notes.dh: אשר לו חומה אע"פ שאין לו עכשיו
notes.he: דלא כתיב והיה לו חומה אלא אשר לו משמע דאפי' היה לו קודם לכן נחשב ערי חומה אלמא קסבר קדושה ראשונה קידשה לשעתה וקדשה לעתיד לבוא:
notes.en: “Which has [lo] a wall,” even though it does not have one now: for it is not written “and it had a wall,” but “which has [lo],” implying that even if it had [one] before, it is counted among walled cities. Evidently he holds that the first consecration sanctified for its time and sanctified for the future.

messages.text: § What is the reasoning of the one who says that the initial consecration of Eretz Yisrael consecrated it for its time, but did not consecrate it forever?

It is written with regard to the return from Babylonia: “And all the congregation of those that were coming back out of the captivity made sukkot, and dwelt in sukkot, for since the days of Joshua, son of Nun, unto that day the children of Israel had not done so. And there was very great joy” (Nehemiah 8:17).

verse.he: וַיַּעֲשׂוּ כׇל־הַקָּהָל הַשָּׁבִים מִן־הַשְּׁבִי ׀ סֻכּוֹת וַיֵּשְׁבוּ בַסֻּכּוֹת כִּי לֹא־עָשׂוּ מִימֵי יֵשׁוּעַ בִּן־נוּן כֵּן בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל עַד הַיּוֹם הַהוּא וַתְּהִי שִׂמְחָה גְּדוֹלָה מְאֹד׃
verse.en: The whole community that returned from the captivity made booths and dwelt in the booths—the Israelites had not done so from the days of Joshua. son of Nun to that day—and there was very great rejoicing.

messages.text: Now, is it possible that King David came and the Jews in his time and all subsequent generations did not make sukkot, until Ezra came?

Rather, when the verse states: “For since the days of Joshua,” it means to compare their arrival in Eretz Yisrael in the days of Ezra to their arrival in the days of Joshua: Just as with regard to their arrival in the days of Joshua, they counted Sabbatical Years and Jubilee Years and they sanctified walled cities, so too, with regard to their arrival in the days of Ezra, they counted Sabbatical Years and Jubilee Years and they sanctified walled cities.

notes.dh: אלא מקיש ביאתם בימי עזרא כו'
notes.he: דהא כי לא עשו לאו אסוכות מהדר אלא הכי קאמר כי לא עשו מה שעשו עכשיו מימות יהושע ומאי ניהו קדושת הארץ:
notes.en: Rather, it compares their arrival in the days of Ezra, and so on: for “they had not done so” does not refer back to the sukkot; rather, this is what it says: they had not done what they did now since the days of Joshua. And what is that? The consecration of the land.

notes.he: שהתחילו למנות שמיטין ונתחייבו במעשר:
notes.en: They counted Sabbatical Years: they began to count Sabbatical Years and became obligated in tithes.

notes.he: פי' לענין מכירת בית בבתי ערי חומה ולענין שילוח מצורעים חוץ לעיר דדוקא בבתי ערי חומה צריך לשלוח המצורעים חוץ לחומה אבל שאר (ארצות) [עיירות] לא ואבנים מנוגעות צריך לשלוח חוץ לעיר ואפי' לא היו מוקפות מימות יהושע והכי תניא בתורת כהנים אתהן חוץ לעיר ואין אדם חוץ לכל העיר אלא חוץ לעיירות המוקפות חומה בלבד וא"ת מנלן הא לא כתיב בית חומה גבי אדם מצורע ואומר הרב רבינו יצחק דגמרינן חוץ למחנה מושבו דכתיב ביה במצורע (ויקרא י״ג:מ״ו) ממושב דכתיב בית מושב עיר חומה (שם כה) ופירש רש"י כאן דמקדש ליה (לארעא) בשתי תודות ובשיר ובית דין מהלכין ושתי תודות אחריהן כדאיתא בשבועות (דף טז. ושם) ובמס' שבועות פירש"י דאשכחן שהיו מקדשין חומות ירושלים בשתי תודות ובשיר כשבאו להוסיף על העיר ועל (העיירות) [העזרות] אבל שאר (ארצות) [עיירות] לא ידעתי היאך היו מקדשין אותן:
notes.en: And they sanctified walled cities: meaning, with regard to the sale of a house among the houses of walled cities, and with regard to sending lepers outside the city. For only in walled cities must lepers be sent outside the wall, but not in other [cities]; whereas afflicted stones must be sent outside the city even if [it] was not surrounded [by a wall] from the days of Joshua. And so it is taught in Torat Kohanim: “them … outside the city” [of the stones]; but a person is not [sent] outside every city, only outside cities surrounded by a wall. And if you say: from where do we derive this? “A walled house” is not written with regard to a leper! Our master Rabbeinu Yitzḥak says that we derive “outside the camp shall his dwelling [moshavo] be,” written of the leper (Leviticus 13:46), from “dwelling” written in “a dwelling house in a walled city” (Leviticus 25:29). And Rashi explains here that it is sanctified with two thanksgiving offerings and with song, and the court walking with two thanksgiving offerings behind them, as in Shevuot (16a). And in tractate Shevuot Rashi explains that we find they would sanctify the walls of Jerusalem with two thanksgiving offerings and with song when they came to add to the city and to the courtyards; but other cities, I do not know how they would sanctify them.

messages.text: And so it says with regard to the return of the Jews from exile: “And the Lord your God will bring you into the land that your fathers possessed, and you shall possess it” (Deuteronomy 30:5).

verse.he: וֶהֱבִיאֲךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ אֶל־הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר־יָרְשׁוּ אֲבֹתֶיךָ וִירִשְׁתָּהּ וְהֵיטִבְךָ וְהִרְבְּךָ מֵאֲבֹתֶיךָ׃
verse.en: And the ETERNAL your God will bring you to the land that your ancestors possessed, and you shall possess it; and you will be made more prosperous and more numerous than your ancestors.

notes.he: בשובם מן הגלות משתעי קרא דכתיב לעיל מיניה (דברים ל) ושב ה' אלהיך את שבותך ורחמך:
notes.en: And the Lord your God will bring you, and so on: the verse speaks of their return from the exile, as it is written just before it (Deuteronomy 30:3): “Then the Lord your God will turn your captivity and have compassion upon you.”

messages.text: The verse compares your possession to the possession of your fathers: Just as the possession of your fathers came with the renewal of all these matters, i.e., the Sabbatical Year and the Jubilee Year, and terumot and tithes, so too your possession comes with the renewal of all these matters, as the initial consecration was nullified.

notes.he: [הללו אלמא] הוצרכו לקדש פעם שניה:
notes.en: With the renewal of all these matters: [evidently] they needed to sanctify a second time.

messages.text: And the tanna who maintains the other opinion, that the initial consecration of Eretz Yisrael is eternal, how does he interpret the verse in Nehemiah? When the verse states: “For since the days of Joshua,” this is not referring to actual sukkot; rather, the verse means that Ezra prayed for mercy with regard to the evil inclination of idol worship and nullified it, and the merit of his prayer protected them like a sukka.

notes.he: לעולם כי לא עשו אסוכות קאי ולאו סוכות ממש אלא דבעא עזרא רחמי איצרא דעבודה זרה ואימסר בידיה כדאמר בסנהדרין (דף סד.):
notes.en: And the other: actually “they had not done so” does refer to the sukkot, but not actual sukkot; rather, Ezra prayed for mercy regarding the inclination of idol worship and it was delivered into his hands, as it says in Sanhedrin (64a).

notes.he: דעזרא עלייהו:
notes.en: And the merit protected: [the merit] of Ezra, over them.

notes.he: כי לא עשו דבר זה בימות יהושע כן והיינו דקפיד קרא לאדכורי יהושע טפי מהאחרים וקא מדכר ליה בלשון גנאי:
notes.en: Like a sukka: for they had not done this thing so in the days of Joshua. And this is why the verse is exacting to mention Joshua more than the others, and mentions him in a derogatory form.

notes.he: מאן דאמר דקידשה נמי לעתיד [לבוא] במאי מוקים ויעשו כל הקהל השבים [סכות וישבו בסכות:
notes.en: And the other: the one who says it sanctified for the future too, how does he explain “And all the congregation of those that were coming back made [sukkot and dwelt in sukkot]”?

notes.he: קסבר לאו סוכות ממש קאמר אלא דאגין זכותיה דעזרא עלייהו כי סוכה משום דבטיל יצרא דע"ז מנייהו כדמפרשי' במס' סנהדרין בפ' ארבע מיתות:
notes.en: He holds that it does not speak of actual sukkot, but that Ezra’s merit protected them like a sukka, because he nullified the inclination of idol worship from them, as we explain in tractate Sanhedrin, in chapter Arba Mitot.

messages.text: And this is the reason that the verse criticizes Joshua for not praying for the removal of this inclination himself. How is this criticism indicated in the verse? As in every other place in the Bible, his name is written as: Yehoshua, and here it is written: Yeshua.

notes.dh: דבכל דוכתא כתיב יהושע והכא ישוע
notes.he: משום דאיהו הוה ליה למיבעי רחמי עלה דמילתא דבשלמא משה לא בעא רחמי כו':
notes.en: For everywhere “Yehoshua” is written, and here “Yeshua”: because he should have prayed for mercy about the matter; for granted, Moses did not pray for mercy, and so on.

messages.text: Granted, Moses, the first leader of the Jewish people, did not pray for mercy that this inclination should be removed, as at the time there was no merit of Eretz Yisrael; but Joshua, who had the merit of Eretz Yisrael, why didn’t he pray for mercy that this inclination should be nullified?

notes.he: דמחסרו וקראו ישוע דלא בעא רחמי ולא בטליה ליצר דע"ז:
notes.en: And this is why the verse is exacting with him: for it shortens [his name] and calls him Yeshua, because he did not pray for mercy and did not nullify the inclination of idol worship.

messages.text: But according to the opinion that the initial consecration was not nullified, isn’t it written: “Which your fathers possessed and you shall possess it”? This verse apparently indicates that it was necessary to sanctify Eretz Yisrael a second time.
messages.quote: compares your possession to the possession of your fathers

messages.text: According to this opinion, this is what the verse is saying: Since your fathers possessed the land, you too possess it, and there is no need to sanctify it again.

notes.he: באותה קדושה ואין צריך לחזור ולקדש:
notes.en: You possess it: with that same sanctity, and there is no need to sanctify it again.

notes.he: ולהאי תנא והכתיב אשר ירשו אבותיך וירשתה דמקיש אף ירושתך בחידוש כל הדברים אלמא דצריכה לקדושי דלא קידשה לעתיד לבוא הכי קאמר. אמר לך הכי דריש לקרא כיון דירשו אבותיך ירשתה אף [אתה] באותה קדושה עצמה ואי אתה צריך לקידוש אחר]:
notes.en: And according to this tanna, isn’t it written “which your fathers possessed and you shall possess it,” comparing: so too your possession comes with the renewal of all the matters, so evidently it needs to be sanctified, since it did not sanctify for the future? This is what it says: he will tell you that he expounds the verse thus: since your fathers possessed it, you [too] possess it with that very same sanctity, and you do not need another consecration.

messages.caption: Did the first consecration of the land last forever? The two views and how each reads the verses.

messages.text: The baraita cited earlier teaches that the Jews began counting the Jubilee Year upon their return from exile. But did they count Sabbatical Years and Jubilee Years in the days of Ezra?

Now, if from the time that the tribe of Reuben and the tribe of Gad and half the tribe of Manasseh were exiled (see I Chronicles 5:26) the counting of Jubilee Years was nullified, despite the fact that a majority of Jews lived in Eretz Yisrael,

verse.he: וַיָּעַר אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת־רוּחַ ׀ פּוּל מֶלֶךְ־אַשּׁוּר וְאֶת־רוּחַ תִּלְּגַת פִּלְנֶסֶר מֶלֶךְ אַשּׁוּר וַיַּגְלֵם לָראוּבֵנִי וְלַגָּדִי וְלַחֲצִי שֵׁבֶט מְנַשֶּׁה וַיְבִיאֵם לַחְלַח וְחָבוֹר וְהָרָא וּנְהַר גּוֹזָן עַד הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה׃ {פ}
verse.en: So the God of Israel roused the spirit of King Pul of Assyria—the spirit of King Tillegath-pilneser of Assyria—and he carried them away, namely, the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, and brought them to Halah, Habor, Hara, and the river Gozan, to this day.

notes.he: בימי סנחריב:
notes.en: When the tribe of Reuben were exiled: in the days of Sennacherib.

messages.text: then in the time of Ezra, about which it is written: “The whole congregation together was 42,360” (Ezra 2:64), would they have counted Jubilee Years?

verse.he: כׇּל־הַקָּהָל כְּאֶחָד אַרְבַּע רִבּוֹא אַלְפַּיִם שְׁלֹשׁ־מֵאוֹת שִׁשִּׁים׃
verse.en: The sum of the entire community was 42,360,

notes.he: דאפי' עישור מישראל לא היו במקומן דהכי גמירי [דלעולם] אין ישראל פחותים מששים ריבוא כ"ש דלא מנו יובלות:
notes.en: The whole congregation together was four myriads [and more]: for not even a tenth of Israel were in their places, as we have a tradition that Israel is never fewer than sixty myriads; all the more so they did not count Jubilees.

messages.text: From the time that the tribe of Reuben and the tribe of Gad and half the tribe of Manasseh were exiled, the counting of Jubilee Years was nullified, as it is stated: “And you shall proclaim liberty throughout the land to all its inhabitants; it shall be a Jubilee for you” (Leviticus 25:10), indicating that the halakhot of the Jubilee Year apply only when all its inhabitants are in Eretz Yisrael, and not when some of them have been exiled.

verse.he: וְקִדַּשְׁתֶּם אֵת שְׁנַת הַחֲמִשִּׁים שָׁנָה וּקְרָאתֶם דְּרוֹר בָּאָרֶץ לְכׇל־יֹשְׁבֶיהָ יוֹבֵל הִוא תִּהְיֶה לָכֶם וְשַׁבְתֶּם אִישׁ אֶל־אֲחֻזָּתוֹ וְאִישׁ אֶל־מִשְׁפַּחְתּוֹ תָּשֻׁבוּ׃
verse.en: and you shall hallow the fiftieth year. You shall proclaim release throughout the land for all its inhabitants. It shall be a jubilee, “ram” or “ram’s horn.” for you: each of you shall return to your holding and each of you shall return to your family.

messages.text: One might have thought that if all the Jews were living in Eretz Yisrael, but they are intermingled, e.g., the tribe of Benjamin is living in the portion of the tribe of Judah, and the tribe of Judah in the portion of the tribe of Benjamin, that the Jubilee Year should be in effect. Therefore, the verse states: “To all its inhabitants,” which teaches that the Jubilee Year applies only when its inhabitants are living according to their proper arrangment, and not when they are intermingled.

notes.he: [והיו מעורבבים בחלוקת שבט יהודה בבנימין:
notes.en: And they were intermingled: in the allotment, the tribe of Judah in Benjamin.

messages.text: How, then, could those who returned from exile have counted the Jubilee Years?

They counted Jubilee Years in order to sanctify Sabbatical Years. That is, at the end of every seven cycles of the Sabbatical Year they would count the fiftieth year as a Jubilee Year, so that the next Sabbatical cycle would begin in its proper time, in the fifty-first year. Nevertheless, the halakhot of the Jubilee Year were not in effect.

notes.he: ודאי יובל לא היה נוהג שיהו עבדים נפטרים משום יובל ולא שדות של מכר חוזרות אבל שמיטין היו נוהגים לשמט כספים ולשמט מזרע וקציר דהא צריכין למנות שנת יובל כדי שיבואו השמיטין במקומן שלסוף ז' שמיטות היו מניחין שנת נ' שלא היו מונין אותה לשמיטה הבאה מפני שהיא ראויה להיות שנת יובל ושנה של אחריה מתחיל המנין דאם לא היו מונין יובלות היו מונין אותה שנה לחשבון השמיטין והוו השמיטין שלא במקומן:
notes.en: They counted Jubilees to sanctify Sabbatical Years: certainly the Jubilee was not in effect, such that slaves would go free because of the Jubilee or sold fields would return; but the Sabbatical Years were in effect, to cancel debts and to cease from sowing and harvesting. For they needed to count the Jubilee year so that the Sabbatical Years would come in their proper place: at the end of seven Sabbatical cycles they would leave aside the fiftieth year and not count it toward the next Sabbatical cycle, since it is fit to be a Jubilee year, and the count begins with the year after it. For if they did not count Jubilees, they would count that year in the reckoning of the Sabbatical cycles, and the Sabbatical Years would fall out of their place.

notes.he: מכאן תימה לברייתא דתני בירושלמי דמסכת גיטין ורש"י כתב בפ' השולח (גיטין דף לו.) דתניא בירושלמי וזה דבר השמיטה שמוט בשתי שמיטות הכתוב מדבר אחד שמיטת יובל ואחד שמיטת שביעית בזמן שאתה משמט [יובל] אתה משמט [שביעית] בזמן שאי אתה משמט יובל אי אתה משמט שביעית וכאן אומר דלא מנו יובלות אלא לקדש שמיטין ופירש רש"י פ' השולח (שם) דההיא דערכין דמדרבנן היא ואין משמע כן בת"כ (ואומר אני דתנאי היא (עכ"ל רש"י) (דהא דירושלמי רבי היא) ועוד אור"ת דהך ברייתא דמייתי) ריש פרק השולח (שם) וזה דבר השמיטה שמוט בשתי שמיטות הכתוב מדבר אחת שמיטת קרקע ואחת שמיטת כספים והא דירושלמי רבי היא אבל רבנן פליגי עליה דרבי ואמרי מנין דיש שמיטה אף על פי שאין יובל ת"ל (ויקרא כ״ה:ח׳) והיו לך שבע שבתות השנים ומנין שיעשה יובל אע"פ שאין שביעית ת"ל (שם) והיו לך תשע וארבעים שנה [וסוגיא] דהכא אתיא כרבנן מיהו יש ליישב ההיא דתורת כהנים אפי' כר' והא דתני שביעית אע"פ שאין יובל יש לפרשה אע"פ שלא נהגו יובל והניחו בחטאם וכדתני בפ"ק דראש השנה (דף ט: ושם) יובל היא אע"פ שלא שמטו ואע"פ שלא תקעו יכול אע"פ שלא שלחו ת"ל היא דברי ר' יהודה רבי יוסי אומר יובל אע"פ שלא שמטו ואע"פ שלא שלחו יכול אף על פי שלא תקעו ת"ל היא:
notes.en: In brief: This raises a difficulty against a baraita in the Jerusalem Talmud, tractate Gittin, which Rashi cites in chapter HaSholeiaḥ (Gittin 36a): “And this is the manner of the remission: remitting”: the verse speaks of two remissions, the remission of the Jubilee and the remission of the Sabbatical Year; when you remit in the Jubilee you remit in the Sabbatical Year, and when you do not remit in the Jubilee you do not remit in the Sabbatical Year. Yet here it says that they counted Jubilees only to sanctify Sabbatical Years [so the Sabbatical Year was observed without the Jubilee]. Rashi explained in HaSholeiaḥ that [the Sabbatical Year spoken of in] Arakhin is rabbinic; but Torat Kohanim does not imply so [a parenthetical adds Rashi’s words: “and I say it is a dispute of tannaim,” since the Jerusalem Talmud’s baraita is Rabbi’s]. Further, Rabbeinu Tam says that the baraita cited at the beginning of HaSholeiaḥ reads the two remissions as the remission of land and the remission of money; the Jerusalem Talmud’s baraita is Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi], and the Rabbis disagree with Rabbi and say: from where is it derived that there is a Sabbatical Year even when there is no Jubilee? The verse states: “And you shall count seven sabbaths of years” (Leviticus 25:8); and from where that one makes a Jubilee even when there is no Sabbatical Year? The verse states: “forty-nine years.” Our passage follows the Rabbis. Still, Torat Kohanim can be reconciled even according to Rabbi: “a Sabbatical Year even when there is no Jubilee” can mean even when they did not observe the Jubilee and stayed in their sin, as taught in Rosh HaShana (9b): “It is a Jubilee” even if they did not release and even if they did not blow the shofar; might it be so even if they did not free [slaves]? The verse says “it is,” the words of Rabbi Yehuda. Rabbi Yosei says: it is a Jubilee even if they did not release and even if they did not free; might it be so even if they did not blow? The verse says “it is.” Open on Sefaria for the full text.

notes.he: יובלות לצורך לקדש שמיטין [לפי שהשמיטין לא בטלו אלא היובלות בלבד ולכך היו מונין יובלות כדי לקדש שמיטין] בזמנן לפי שאין שנת היובל בחשבון שני השבוע לפיכך הוצרכו למנות ולידע מתי הוא יובל לפי שאחר ז' שמיטין הוא יובל ויש להן לעשות שמיטה שמינית לאחר ח' (ימים) [שנים] לפי שאין שנת יובל עולה לחשבון השמיטה:
notes.en: [The text here reads “Rav Yitzḥak said”; the daf has Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak.] They counted Jubilees for the need of sanctifying Sabbatical Years, [since the Sabbatical Years were not nullified, only the Jubilees, and so they would count Jubilees in order to sanctify Sabbatical Years] in their time. Since the Jubilee year is not counted among the years of the seven-year cycle, they needed to count and to know when the Jubilee is, since the Jubilee comes after seven Sabbatical cycles, and they must make the eighth Sabbatical Year after eight years, since the Jubilee year does not count toward the Sabbatical reckoning.

messages.text: Continues on 33a: the Gemara asks how this works according to Rabbi Yehuda, who holds that the fiftieth year counts for both cycles.
